subject: Stewardship microgrant pilot request — OpenForge hack sprint
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane@openforge.org>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stewardship microgrant pilot request — OpenForge hack sprint

Hi Diego + Marissa,

Thanks for taking a look. OpenForge is running a community hack sprint (Oct 8-10) focused on education tooling for underrepresented contributors. We maintain a small group of ~300 active maintainers and typically have 80-120 attendees for the sprint.

We'd love to request a microgrant in the form of free credits or a short trial extension to power workshop demos and mentor sessions. Our ask:~
- 120k token-equivalent credits (to cover workshops + demo bots)
- A 90-day trial extension for the repo-level test environment

Attached is a short scope doc that outlines expected usage patterns and attendee count. We can provide proof of openness (MIT/Apache) and a short post-event writeup.

Are there standard pilot packages you recommend for community-run sprints? Happy to jump on a quick call to align.

Best,
Jane Park
Program Lead — OpenForge
https://openforge.org

Attachment: openforge_scope.pdf

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane@openforge.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stewardship microgrant pilot request — OpenForge hack sprint

Hi Jane — thanks for the note and scope doc, appreciate the context. Quick clarifying questions so we can route this efficiently: 

1) When you say "120k token-equivalent credits", is that conservative (peak) or a target usage estimate over the 90-day window?
2) Do you need a promo code (redeemable in the hosted API) or would you prefer dedicated trial capacity we can reserve for the sprint days?
3) Any compliance or enterprise constraints we should be aware of (e.g., need for SOC2 evidence or specific data retention settings)?

Internally looping in Rishi to weigh in on promotional allowances and Marissa on community programs. If it helps, we often do a staged pilot: smaller promo code to cover demos + mentor hours, then a top-up if usage ramps.

If you can send a short expected request by participant/workshop (rough numbers), we can draft an approval path today.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Manager, Community Programs
Redwood Inference

- Recommend approving an initial pilot of 50k token credits + 2 mentor office-hours (Redwood engineers) as a lightweight package.
- Ask OpenForge for an attendee roster and a simple acceptance of our community terms (one-paragraph).
- For the 90-day extension: we can do that but prefer the promo-code route to keep accounting clear.

If Rishi is good with the numbers I can draft the promo code and communications for the community page.

Thanks Diego / Marissa — apologies for the terse original ask, mea culpa.

Short answers: 
- 120k was an upper-bound estimate assuming large workshop usage; the core demo + mentor load looks closer to 45k-60k tokens over the sprint days.
- Promo code is ideal (makes it easy for attendees to redeem on hosted API).
- No enterprise constraints; we can accept standard community terms. We will share a final attendee roster by Sep 30.

Attaching a preliminary attendee CSV and a one-pager for the sponsor blurb. If you can approve a 50k pilot promo code and a small mentor hour allocation that would be perfect — we'll surface results publicly and add Redwood to the sponsor banner.

Appreciate it —
Jane Park
Program Lead — OpenForge
Attachment: hacksprint_roster.csv

Jane — great, thanks for the clarification and the roster. We can approve the pilot as follows: 

- Promo code: PRJ-OPENF-50K (redeemable for 50,000 token-equivalent free credits; expires 90 days from issuance)
- Two mentor office-hours (Redwood engineer on call for workshop troubleshooting)
- We ask that OpenForge publish a short acknowledgement (one paragraph) post-event and send usage numbers for a brief post-mortem.

I've included the promo code in the attachment for internal tracking. Marissa — will you publish the community blurb and make the code available to Jane when billing confirms issuance? Rishi — please confirm budget OK and I'll route to billing to create the promo code formally (HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/OF-48291).

Next steps:
- Rishi to confirm by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa to prepare community comms once billing confirms.
- Jane to share final attendee list by Sep 30.

Thanks — excited to support OpenForge.

Diego Fernandez
Manager, Community Programs
Redwood Inference
